bio.text: Josh Kaul, a Democrat, was sworn in as Wisconsin's 45th Attorney General on January 7, 2019, and is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for re-election after advancing from the August 11 Democratic primary.
He earned a bachelor's degree in economics and history from Yale University in 2003 and a law degree from Stanford Law School in 2006, then clerked for U.S. Circuit Judge Michael Boudin.
Kaul worked at Jenner & Block from 2007 to 2010, was an assistant U.S. attorney in the District of Maryland from 2010 to 2014, and joined Perkins Coie as a voting rights attorney in 2014.
